subject.title: feat: add provider sign-in to macOS AI onboarding

question: Should the macOS first-run flow become a generic interactive client for provider-owned OAuth and device-code methods through an additive Crestodian/gateway protocol?
rationale: The change adds user-facing setup capability and public plugin/gateway auth contracts, and the protected maintainer label requires explicit agreement on the security boundary, portable prompt model, and initial provider scope.

options.title: Sponsor generic bridge
options.body: Approve a provider-owned interactive-auth descriptor and gateway session rendered by one reusable macOS sheet, with compatibility and end-to-end proof requirements.

options.title: Pilot narrower scope
options.body: Approve the generic contract but initially expose only providers whose login method is remote-safe and fully proven on signed macOS builds.

options.title: Remain terminal-first
options.body: Keep OAuth and device-code login in CLI setup, leaving native onboarding limited to detected sessions and app-guided secrets.

recommendation.title: Sponsor generic bridge
recommendation.body: Approve a provider-owned interactive-auth descriptor and gateway session rendered by one reusable macOS sheet, with compatibility and end-to-end proof requirements.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently maintained the fresh Mac provider-login setup path and supplied the concrete product scope for this issue.
